title: Filtered Ind extension from compact generators
statement: Use the universes, coherent categories, Yoneda embedding and filtered completion $j:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ of [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], local smallness, $\kappa$-filtered colimits, $\kappa$-compactness, presentability and colimit preservation from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent functor categories, fully faithful functors, functor equivalences and replete full subcategories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $\mathcal C$ be a small infinity category, and let $\mathcal D$ be a locally small infinity category admitting small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Restriction along $j$ gives an equivalence from the full coherent functor category on functors $\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal D$ preserving small $\kappa$-filtered colimits to $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)$. In particular every $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ has an essentially unique such extension $F$, with $Fj\simeq f$. If $f$ is fully faithful and each $f(c)$ is $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal D$, then $F$ is fully faithful and induces an equivalence onto its replete full essential image; if in addition every object of $\mathcal D$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects $f(c)$, then $F$ is an equivalence. If $\mathcal C$ admits all $\kappa$-small colimits, $\mathcal D$ is presentable, and $f$ preserves $\kappa$-small colimits, then $F$ preserves all small colimits.

source.place: HTT Propositions 5.3.5.10 and 5.3.5.11, printed pp. 406-407; equivalence criterion 1.2.10.1; the all-colimit extension clause follows from Corollary 5.3.5.4 (p. 404), by the right adjoint d |-> Map_D(f(-),d), and is also the generator formulation used in Proposition 5.5.1.9 (pp. 461-462).

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ and $u:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$. First put the possibly non-cocomplete target in a cocomplete category. Choose an auxiliary universe $\mathcal V$ containing $\mathcal D$ and its mapping spaces, without changing the meaning of small ($\mathcal U$-small), and form $\widehat{\mathcal D}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})^{\mathrm{op}}$ in a still larger ambient universe. Opposite Yoneda $e(d)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d,-)$ is fully faithful by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied to $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the auxiliary universes. The same node supplies objectwise small limits in the functor category, hence small colimits in its opposite. For any existing small colimit cocone in $\mathcal D$, its image under $e$ is colimiting: at each testing object this says that a contravariant representable takes that colimit to a limit. Conversely, if its image is colimiting, evaluation at every $d$ gives exactly the mapping-space criterion for that cocone to be colimiting in $\mathcal D$. Replace $\mathcal D$ by its replete full essential image under $e$, using [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to transport along the equivalence when necessary. This image is closed under every small colimit that exists in $\mathcal D$, in particular under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Only the ambient universe is enlarged; no larger filtered colimits in the original target are assumed.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.5.7, printed p. 405; opposite Yoneda construction, expanded using Propositions 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.3.2.

proof.text: For $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] supplies a small-colimit-preserving $H:\mathcal P(\mathcal C)\to\widehat{\mathcal D}$ and $Hj\simeq ef$. Given $X\in\mathcal I$, choose a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i\in J}j(c_i)$ from [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability]. Then $H(X)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i e f(c_i)\simeq e(\operatorname{colim}_i f(c_i))$, by preservation by $H$ and by $e$ from step 1. Thus every vertex of $Hu$ lies in the replete full image of $e$. Fullness makes this a coherent factorization, not just a choice of vertex values: every simplex of $Hu$ has its vertices in that full subcategory. Its quasi-inverse from [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] gives $F:\mathcal I\to\mathcal D$ and $eF\simeq Hu$, with $Fj\simeq f$. For any small $\kappa$-filtered colimit cocone in $\mathcal I$, $u$ preserves it by [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability] and $H$ preserves it. Hence $eF$ preserves it; reflection by $e$ from step 1 proves that $F$ preserves it as well.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.5.8(1) and its proof, printed pp. 405-406; extension into the auxiliary cocomplete target and restriction to the Ind subcategory.

proof.text: Let $G:\mathcal I\to\mathcal D$ be any small-$\kappa$-filtered-colimit-preserving functor. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-intermediate-presheaf-kan] with intermediate full subcategory $\mathcal I$, cocomplete target $\widehat{\mathcal D}$, extension $H$ of step 2, and functor $eG$. It identifies the full space of transformations $Hu\to eG$ with the space of transformations $ef\to eGj$. Passing through the equivalence of $\mathcal D$ with its full image identifies these spaces with $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(f,Gj)$ respectively: for a literal full subcategory the equality of the transformation simplicial sets follows degree by degree from the definition of $\operatorname{Fun}$, since all vertices of $\mathcal I\times\Delta^n$ land in that subcategory. Now take $f=Gj$. The identity on $Gj$ extends to a comparison $\alpha:F\to G$. Each $X$ has the filtered presentation in step 2, and both functors preserve its cocone, so $\alpha_X$ is the map of colimits induced by the pointwise equivalence $\alpha_{j(c_i)}$. It is an equivalence. Pointwise detection from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], in a sufficiently large ambient universe, makes $\alpha$ a functor equivalence. Therefore every filtered-colimit-preserving functor is equivalent to a constructed $F$, and the displayed mapping-space equivalence proves full faithfulness of restriction for every pair of such functors. Step 2 proves essential surjectivity. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to restriction yields the asserted equivalence of coherent functor categories. Its fiber over $f$ is consequently contractible, giving essential uniqueness with the comparison $Fj\simeq f$ included.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.5.8(2) and Proposition 5.3.5.10, printed p. 406; the Kan-extension mapping property and the filtered-generation comparison.

proof.text:
Suppose now that $f$ is fully faithful and its values are $\kappa$-compact. Present $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i\in J}j(c_i)$ and $Y\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{t\in L}j(d_t)$ with $J,L$ small and $\kappa$-filtered. The mapping-space colimit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], compactness of $j(c_i)$ in [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], and compactness of $f(c_i)$ as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal I}(X,Y)\simeq\lim_{i\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{colim}_{t\in L}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c_i,d_t),\qquad
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(FX,FY)\simeq\lim_{i\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{colim}_{t\in L}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(f(c_i),f(d_t)).$$
Here $F$ preserves the two chosen colimits by step 2, and $j$ is fully faithful by [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability]. Under these natural identifications the comparison induced by $F$ is the limit of the colimits of the comparisons induced by $f$. Those comparisons are equivalences by full faithfulness of $f$; functors on spaces preserve equivalences. Hence $F$ is fully faithful. There is no interchange of a limit with a colimit in this argument.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.11(1), printed p. 407; the two successive compact-generator reductions written as a mapping-space formula.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], the fully faithful $F$ of step 4 induces an equivalence $\mathcal I\simeq\mathcal D_0$, where $\mathcal D_0$ is its replete full essential image. If every object $d$ of $\mathcal D$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of values $f(c)$, the entire diagram presenting $d$ factors through $\mathcal D_0$: it is a full subcategory and every vertex belongs to it. Compose this coherent diagram with a quasi-inverse $\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal I$, take its small $\kappa$-filtered colimit in $\mathcal I$ (which exists by [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability]), and apply $F$. Preservation from step 2 shows that the result is equivalent to $d$. Thus $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D$ and $F$ is an equivalence. This also explains why objectwise membership in the image suffices here: fullness and its quasi-inverse supply the whole lifted diagram.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.11(2), printed pp. 407-408; lift the generating diagram to the full essential image before taking its colimit.

proof.text: For the last clause assume that $\mathcal C$ has all $\kappa$-small colimits, that $\mathcal D$ is presentable, and that $f$ preserves those colimits. Fix $d\in\mathcal D$ and form the coherent small-space-valued presheaf $R_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(f(c),d)$. The coherent representable presheaf in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], precomposed with $f^{\mathrm{op}}$, supplies this presheaf; local smallness gives its small values. For a $\kappa$-small colimit cocone $q\to c$ in $\mathcal C$, preservation by $f$ and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give $R_d(c)\simeq\lim R_d(q(-))$. For the empty shape this says $R_d(0_{\mathcal C})\simeq *$, since $f(0_{\mathcal C})$ is initial. Thus the exact condition (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-ind-criterion] holds, and $R_d$ is an object of $\mathcal I$. No compactness or full faithfulness of $f$ is used in this final clause.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, printed p. 404, implication (3) to (1); apply to the presheaf of maps from f(-) to d, including the empty limit.

proof.text:
There is a canonical natural comparison
$$\tau_{X,d}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(FX,d)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(\mathcal C)}(X,R_d).$$
To specify it, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] identifies a map $FX\to d$ with a coherent transformation $h_{FX}\to h_d$ on $\mathcal D$. Precompose it with $f^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then with the transformation $h_X\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}\to h_{FX}\circ f^{\mathrm{op}}$ induced by $F$ and $Fj\simeq f$. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation], $h_X\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq X$, naturally in $X$. This specifies $\tau$ coherently on the full mapping spaces and makes it natural in $X$ and $d$. For $X=j(c)$ it is the Yoneda equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(\mathcal C)}(j(c),R_d)\simeq R_d(c)$, with its direction reversed. For $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i j(c_i)$ as in step 2, both sides take this colimit to the limit of their values on the $j(c_i)$: the left side by preservation by $F$ and the representable-colimit formula; the right side because the inclusion $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ preserves these colimits. The natural map $\tau_{X,d}$ is therefore a limit of equivalences and is an equivalence. Fullness of $\mathcal I$ identifies its right side with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal I}(X,R_d)$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4 and the mapping-space proof of Proposition 5.3.5.11, printed pp. 404 and 407; agent-expanded canonical comparison for the all-colimit clause.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], the hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ implies that $\mathcal I$ admits all small colimits. Let $p:J\to\mathcal I$ be any small coherent diagram and let $p\to X$ be a colimit cocone. For every $d\in\mathcal D$, the natural equivalence of step 7 and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(FX,d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal I}(X,R_d)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal I}(p(j),R_d)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fp(j),d).$$
Naturality of $\tau$ identifies this equivalence with the comparison induced by the actual image cocone $Fp\to FX$. The mapping-space colimit criterion therefore proves that this image cocone is colimiting. This holds for every small shape, including the empty one, and proves that $F$ preserves all small colimits.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, printed p. 404, with the representable mapping-space colimit criterion; all-colimit consequence used in Proposition 5.5.1.9, printed pp. 461-462.
